questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The surrounding nature of Bergen facilitated a great learning environment. Furthermore, I've heard good things about UiB, both the academic level, but also the social aspects.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to live with strangers, but be open to meeting new people with different cultural and social backgrounds.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at UiB harmonized with the process at my own university. It was easy and straightforward. If i had any questions, even regarding my courses, the study guides was very helpfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both via telephone, but also E-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very sucessful. I applied for 3 courses on 3 different faculties - whereas 1 of thoose was restricted and didnt harmonize with my field of study. I got accepted at all 3.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open to new courses that you wouldnt normally take at your home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *

Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses was on the same academic level as in my home university, however, the mandatory - qualifying assignments was definitely more demanding.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only had classes at the auditoriums, which i havent had at UCPH in a long time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Artificial Intelligence on philosophy - since it is very relevant in this age of AI. The course gives an insight into the world of AI with an interesting philosophical standpoint.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on hikes through the beautiful nature of Norway. Plan your trips ahead, and book a cabin through DNT.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature and other cities of Norway.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and curious - it reflects.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As a Danish exchange student, it was clear to see an age gap between danish, and other students across the world. In Denmark, people are usually a few years older than the student at other places.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the love and happiness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the prices. Things are very expensive. 
Be open to new adventures. Explore the nature of Norway. 
Sign up to different activities that you wouldnt do in your own country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I lived at a student housing through SAMMEN. Be prepared to plan how long you are going to stay beforehand, since they require you to terminate your contract in 3 months advance.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic level, the courses and nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The price on groceries and basic living.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
